transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Got it, thanks for calling in — missing calls when you’re out on jobs is exactly what we focus on.  

When a call comes in and you’re out on a job, what usually happens to that caller — does it go to voicemail, or do they just end up calling the next company?
User: The calls usually go to voicemail.
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — so most of these are just rolling to voicemail.  

Do people actually leave messages, or do you feel like a lot of those callers just move on to the next company instead?
User: About 50% would book if someone answered, but many likely move on to the next company.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — if half of those could’ve booked, that’s a lot of work walking away just because no one could pick up.  

So roughly how many calls a week do you think are hitting voicemail instead of a live person?
User: About 8 calls a week go to voicemail instead of reaching someone live.
Agent: Got it — 8 calls a week hitting voicemail is more than most people realize.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those missed calls are actually costing you in lost jobs?
User: No, not specifically, but I know missed calls do impact potential job bookings.
Agent: Got it, you’re already aware it’s hurting bookings, just haven’t seen it in black-and-white yet.  

So ballpark, what’s your average job worth for you — are we talking closer to $300, $500, $800 per job?
User: Our average job value is about $2,500.
Agent: Right, so with 8 missed calls a week, 50% of those ready to book, and $2,500 a job, you’re leaving around $43K a month on the table just from calls going to voicemail.  

So… would it be helpful to see a quick walkthrough this week of how we can turn those after-hours and on-job calls into booked jobs instead of voicemails?
User: Yes, I'd be interested in a walkthrough to see how we can convert those missed calls into jobs.
Agent: Nice, that makes sense — if we can turn even a chunk of that $43K into booked jobs, it’s a big win.  

So first thing, what’s your first name?
User: I'm Susan, but let's focus on scheduling the live call.
Agent: Got it Susan, we’ll keep this simple and focused on getting that live call set up.  

Quick thing before we look at times — what’s your last name?
User: Let's schedule the live call. I'm more interested in that than personal details right now.
Agent: Totally hear you — the goal is that live call, not a long form. We just need a couple basics so we can actually book it on the calendar.  

Since we already have your first name, what’s the name of your company?
User: My company is Cornerstone Remodeling.
Agent: Cornerstone Remodeling, perfect — that helps me line things up correctly.  

Quick check, Susan — what’s your last name so we know who Jay will be speaking with on that walkthrough?
User: Let's just say Susan for now. I'm interested in scheduling the walkthrough.
Agent: Got it Susan, we can absolutely book it under Susan and Cornerstone Remodeling.  

So… for that walkthrough with Jay, would you prefer later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better.
Agent: Makes sense, tomorrow works.  

I’ve got availability next on Thursday the 27th with a few afternoon and early evening times — would something around 3:30 PM Eastern or closer to 5 PM Eastern work better for your 20‑minute walkthrough?
User: 3:30 PM Eastern works for me.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Thanks Susan — you’re all set for Thursday the 27th at 3:30 PM Eastern with Jay. You’ll get an SMS confirmation with all the details, and you can tap to add it to your calendar or reschedule if something comes up.

Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?

Alright, really glad you called in. Jay’s looking forward to walking through how we can turn those missed calls into booked remodeling jobs. Have a great rest of your day — bye!
